column3: Close to the Hebrew; “he turns his hand all the day” is rendered “Time and time again throughout the day.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he has made to waste away” is rendered “He has aged.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he has built against me” is rendered “He has besieged me,” and “poison and hardship” “bitterness and woe.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my bronze fetter” is rendered “my chain.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the sons of his quiver” is rendered “the arrows of His quiver,” and “my kidneys” “my loins.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a laughingstock” is rendered “the ridicule.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he has made me cower in ashes” is rendered “covered me with ashes.”
NKJV renders the third person (“and it has excluded my soul from peace”) as a second-person address, “You have moved my soul far from peace,” and “good” as “prosperity.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my endurance” is rendered “My strength.”
Close to the Hebrew; “it bows down on me” is rendered “sinks within me.”
Close to the Hebrew; “I will wait” is rendered “I have hope.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the covenant loyalties of Yahweh, for we have not come to an end” is rendered “Through the LORD’S mercies we are not consumed.”
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “God” as the subject of “has laid it on him.”
